name: OPA2182IDR
title: 36-V, 5-MHz, low-noise, zero-drift precision op amps with MUX-friendly inputs (single, dual, quad)
summary: OPA182, OPA2182 and OPA4182 are single, dual and quad zero-drift op amps for 4.5 V to 36 V supplies: offset 4 µV at most, drift 0.003 µV/°C typical, 5.7 nV/√Hz noise with no flicker corner, 5 MHz gain-bandwidth and 10 V/µs slew. The output reaches within millivolts of each rail and the input range takes in the negative rail. A switched input stage keeps bias current low under large differential steps, such as multiplexer switching, and a start-up circuit blocks inrush as the supplies come up; the range is –40 °C to 125 °C.
key_figures: 5.7 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz; 0.119 µVPP 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz

circuits.title: Strain-gauge bridge amplifier with analog linearization
circuits.description: Both halves of one OPA2182 on ±18 V. Channel B is a difference amplifier across the bridge's two signal corners: 10 kΩ into each input, 3.4 MΩ from the output back to the inverting input and 3.4 MΩ from the non-inverting input to ground through 2 kΩ and 18 kΩ, both returned to ground. The bridge is excited by a 5 V source between its top corner and ground, and its bottom corner is held by channel A, a voltage follower. The follower's input is the output divided by 115 kΩ over 20 kΩ, so part of the output is fed back into the bridge excitation; that feedback is what straightens the bridge's nonlinear response.

parts.note: EXC+ top corner, EXC- bottom corner, S1 and S2 the signal corners

circuits.title: 24-bit load-cell signal chain with a two-amplifier instrumentation amplifier and ADS1225
circuits.description: A six-wire load cell excited from 5 V feeds a two-op-amp instrumentation amplifier made of two OPAx182 running from +15 V and ground. Each amplifier has 10 kΩ in parallel with 1 µF from output to inverting input, and 50 Ω joins the two inverting inputs, setting the gain by G = 1 + 2·RF/RG; the capacitors band-limit the stage. Each output passes through 1 kΩ to an ADS1225 input, with 10 µF from each input to ground and 1 µF across the pair. The cell's sense lines, through their trace resistance, become the converter's reference: +SENSE to VREFP and -SENSE to VREFN, with 0.1 nF from each to ground and 0.1 µF between them. A host on 3 V drives START and SCLK and reads DRDY/DOUT.

parts.note: six-wire bridge: excitation, sense and output pairs

notes: The excitation is 5 V and both bridge outputs sit near VEX / 2.
The ADS1225 converts at 100 SPS with single-cycle settling.

circuits.title: Programmable ±25 V power supply with OPA548 output stage
circuits.description: A composite amplifier that multiplies a ±5 V DAC8581 output by five to give ±25 V. The OPAx182 on ±15 V takes the DAC voltage on its non-inverting input and drives an OPA548 on ±30 V through 10 kΩ. The OPA548 has 40 kΩ from its output to its inverting input, 10 kΩ from there to ground and 500 nF across the 40 kΩ. The OPAx182's inverting input connects through 1 kΩ to that same node, with 500 nF from its inverting input to its output. The circuit drives a wide range of capacitive and current loads.

circuits.title: Pt100 RTD amplifier with linearization, 0 V to 5 V for 0 °C to 200 °C
circuits.description: A REF5050 fed from 15 V makes a 5 V reference, with 1 µF on its input and on its output. The reference drives a Pt100 to ground through 4.99 kΩ, and the RTD voltage goes to the OPAx182's non-inverting input. The inverting input sits on a divider of 49.1 kΩ from the reference and 1 kΩ to ground, with 60.4 kΩ of feedback from the output, which offsets and scales the reading so the output is 0 V at 0 °C and 5 V at 200 °C. 105.8 kΩ from the output back to the RTD node adds excitation current that rises with the output, correcting the RTD's curvature.

parts.note: positive feedback that linearizes the output

where.Kp(P): bridge sensitivity at normalized pressure P, in mV/V
where.P: pressure as a fraction of the sensor's range, 0 to 1

equations.name: Linearized system output
equations.expr: Vout(P) = (VOS + Vref × G × Kp(P)) / (1 − G × Klin × Kp(P))

where.Kp(P): bridge sensitivity at normalized pressure P, in mV/V

equations.name: Linearization factor
equations.expr: Klin = 4 × Bv × Vref / ((Vout_high − Vout_low) − 2 × Bv × (Vout_high + Vout_low))

equations.name: Output at full load
equations.expr: Vout_high = (VOS + Vref × G × Kp(1)) / (1 − G × Klin × Kp(1))

equations.name: Output at no load
equations.expr: Vout_low = (VOS + Vref × G × Kp(0)) / (1 − G × Klin × Kp(0))
equations.note: The left-hand side should read Vout_low, the output at no load.

equations.name: Offset eliminated
equations.expr: Vout_high × (1 − G × Klin × Kp(1)) − Vref × G × Kp(1) = Vout_low × (1 − G × Klin × Kp(0)) − Vref × G × Kp(0)

equations.name: System gain
equations.expr: G = (Vout_high − Vout_low) / (Kp(1) × (Klin × Vout_high + Vref) − Kp(0) × (Klin × Vout_low + Vref))

equations.name: Offset term
equations.expr: VOS = Vout_low × (1 − G × Klin × Kp(0)) − Vref × G × Kp(0)

where.RG: resistor between the two inverting inputs

operation.text: OPA182 is one amplifier (SOIC-8 or SOT-23-5), OPA2182 two (SOIC-8 or VSSOP-8) and OPA4182 four (SOIC-14; a TSSOP-14 is in preview). Nominal body sizes: SOIC-8 4.90 mm × 3.90 mm, SOT-23-5 2.90 mm × 1.60 mm, VSSOP-8 3.00 mm × 3.00 mm, SOIC-14 8.65 mm × 3.91 mm, TSSOP-14 5.00 mm × 4.40 mm. All are specified from –40 °C to 125 °C.

A zero-drift (chopper) amplifier: switches at the input, run from an internal clock, correct the offset and its drift continuously, so offset stays tiny over temperature and time and the noise is flat to dc with no 1/f region. Distortion is lowest for signals below the chopping frequency. Inside are a 36-V differential front end, three transconductance stages (GM1 to GM3) with compensation capacitors, slew-boost circuitry and ripple-reduction circuitry. The output swings rail to rail, the input range reaches 0.1 V below the negative rail, and the parts are stable at unity gain.
A controlled start-up circuit stops inrush current while the supply rails ramp up.
The output does not reverse when an input is driven beyond the common-mode range: it stays at the rail it was driven toward.

operation.topic: Clock feedthrough on the input bias current
operation.text: Charge injected by the input switches puts brief spikes on the input bias current. They are too short to be amplified but can reach the output through the feedback network; a low-pass RC filter is the most effective way to keep them off the output.

The inputs carry built-in EMI filters. EMIRR +IN, the rejection with RF applied to the non-inverting input, is characterized from 10 MHz to 6 GHz; the inverting input behaves nearly the same, and dual and quad versions match closely. Below the 5 MHz gain-bandwidth an interfering signal falls inside the amplifier's bandwidth.

Steering diodes run from each input and the output to internal supply lines, which meet at an edge-triggered absorption circuit that clamps the voltage across the rails once it passes a threshold above the normal operating voltage and below breakdown. In normal use none of this conducts. If an input rises 500 mV or more above V+, an upper diode conducts into V+ when that supply can sink current; the input current should be held to 10 mA, for which about 5 kΩ in series with the input is suggested under overvoltage. If the supply cannot sink, the input can end up powering the amplifier and pull the rail past its absolute maximum. With the supplies at 0 V, high-impedance rails let the input source supply the amplifier through the diodes (not a normal bias state), and low-impedance rails can let large current flow, limited by the source and its series resistance. When the supply may not absorb the current, TVS (Zener) diodes on the supply pins are used, with a breakdown above the normal supply but low enough to protect: 40 V > VTVSBR(min) > V+.

There are no antiparallel protection diodes across the inputs. A switched-input stage keeps the input bias current small and the input impedance high when a large differential voltage appears, as on a large step, a multiplexer channel change, or use as a comparator, so input RC filters are not disturbed. With slew boost and the wide bandwidth this gives fast settling. Comparator use is allowed, within the absolute maximum limits on input voltage, which are set by the supply rails for both the differential and the common-mode case.
There is one functional mode. The part operates from 4.5 V (±2.25 V) to 36 V (±18 V); above 40 V across the supplies it can be damaged permanently. Many specifications hold from –40 °C to 125 °C.
Place a low-ESR 0.1-µF ceramic capacitor from each supply pin to ground, close to the device; with a single supply, V+ alone needs one. Noisy or high-impedance supplies make this necessary.

Use ground planes and keep analog and digital grounds apart, watching where ground current flows. Route input traces away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles where they must cross. Place the feedback and gain resistors right next to the inverting input pin, and make input traces as short as possible. Leakage into sensitive traces drops with a guard ring held at a low impedance. Clean the board after assembly; water-based cleaning leaves moisture in the package, removed by 30 minutes at 85 °C. For the lowest offset, avoid thermoelectric junctions of dissimilar metals, keep the part thermally isolated from heat sources, and shield it and its input circuit from moving air. The layout example, a difference amplifier in SOIC-8, puts the bypass capacitors right at the pins without vias, surrounds the input pairs with ground pour, and keeps components close to the device and to each other.

The bridge is modelled as a multiplier of excitation and sensitivity; feeding part of the output back into the excitation through the factor Klin cancels the bridge's curvature. The three unknowns are found from the sensor's sensitivity at three points: zero, half and full scale. For a sensor with Kp of 0.0003, 0.0017 and 0.00289 mV/V (about 4% nonlinear) the solution is Klin = 0.173913, G = 323.8178 and VOS = –0.48573; in simulation the corrected output runs in a straight line over 0 V to 5 V, with residual error near ±0.1%. The amplifier is used within the output range given under the open-loop gain conditions, and is chosen for low noise, low offset and enough open-loop gain.

OPA2182 sections serve a Rogowski-coil current measurement for a protection relay as gain stage, integrator, level shifter and buffer for a 2.5 V reference (LM4040AIM3-2.5). There are two paths: a precision path (amplifier, integrator, level shifter) and a fast-settling path (integrator, amplifier, level shifter) for catching short-circuit transients. Power comes from a 5 V input through an LP2951ACSD LDO, with a TPS60403 charge pump and TPS72325 LDO making –2.5 V. Low offset and drift cut calibration, and noise that is flat down to dc helps repeatability over the coil's current range.
